```luau
--- Base type for values that can be stored in inputs. Provides
--- functions for checking the underlying value type.
declare extern type DataValue with

    --- Returns true if the value is a number.
    --- ```lua
    --- local dv: DataValueNumber = DataValue.number()
    --- print(dv.isNumber) -- true
    --- ```
    function isNumber(self): boolean

    --- Returns true if the value is a string.
    --- ```lua
    --- local dv: DataValueNumber = DataValue.number()
    --- print(dv.isString) -- false
    --- ```
    function isString(self): boolean

    --- Returns true if the value is a boolean.
    --- ```lua
    --- local dv: DataValueNumber = DataValue.number()
    --- print(dv.isBoolean) -- false
    --- ```
    function isBoolean(self): boolean

    --- Returns true if the value is a color.
    --- ```lua
    --- local dv: DataValueNumber = DataValue.number()
    --- print(dv.isColor) -- false
    --- ```
    function isColor(self): boolean
end

--- `DataValue` that stores a number value.
declare extern type DataValueNumber extends DataValue with

    --- The stored numeric value.
    --- ```lua
    --- local dv: DataValueNumber = DataValue.number()
    --- dv.value = 200
    --- ```
    value: number
end


--- `DataValue` that stores a string value.
declare extern type DataValueString extends DataValue with

    --- The stored string value.
    --- ```lua
    --- local dv: DataValueString = DataValue.string()
    --- dv.value = "I heart Rive."
    --- ```
    value: string
end

--- `DataValue` that stores a boolean value.
declare extern type DataValueBoolean extends DataValue with

    --- The stored boolean value.
    --- ```lua
    --- local dv: DataValueBoolean = DataValue.boolean()
    --- dv.value = false
    --- ```
    value: boolean
end

--- `DataValue` that stores a color value encoded as a number, with
--- red, green, blue, and alpha components.
declare extern type DataValueColor extends DataValue with

    --- The full color value encoded as a number.
    --- ```lua
    --- local dv: DataValueColor = DataValue.color()
    --- dv.value = Color.rgba(255, 0, 0, 155)
    --- ```
    value: number

    --- Color components in the range [0, 255].
    --- ```lua
    --- local data = DataValue.color()
    --- data.value = Color.rgba(128, 55, 12, 1)
    ---
    --- print(data.red) -- 128
    --- data.red = 233
    --- ```
    red: number

    --- Color components in the range [0, 255].
    --- ```lua
    --- local data = DataValue.color()
    --- data.value = Color.rgba(128, 55, 12, 1)
    ---
    --- print(data.green) -- 55
    --- data.green = 233
    --- ```
    green: number

    --- Color components in the range [0, 255].
    --- ```lua
    --- local data = DataValue.color()
    --- data.value = Color.rgba(128, 55, 12, 1)
    ---
    --- print(data.blue) -- 12
    --- data.blue = 233
    --- ```
    blue: number

    --- Alpha component in the range [0, 255].
    --- ```lua
    --- local data = DataValue.color()
    --- data.value = Color.rgba(128, 55, 12, 1)
    ---
    --- print(data.alpha) -- 1
    --- data.alpha = 255
    --- ```
    alpha: number
end

--- Constructors for `DataValue` types. Each function returns a mutable
--- DataValue container of the corresponding underlying type.
declare DataValue: {

    --- Creates a `DataValueNumber` that stores a number.
    --- ```lua
    --- local data = DataValue.number()
    --- data.value = 42
    ---
    --- print(data.value) -- 42
    --- ```
    number: @checked () -> DataValueNumber,

    --- Creates a `DataValueString` that stores a string.
     --- ```lua
    --- local data = DataValue.string()
    --- data.value = 'Rive for life!'
    ---
    --- print(data.value) -- Rive for life!
    --- ```
    string: @checked () -> DataValueString,

    --- Creates a `DataValueBoolean` that stores a boolean.
     --- ```lua
    --- local data = DataValue.boolean()
    --- data.value = false
    ---
    --- print(data.value) -- false
    --- ```
    boolean: @checked () -> DataValueBoolean,

    --- Creates a `DataValueColor` that stores a `Color`.
     --- ```lua
    --- local data = DataValue.color()
    --- data.value = Color.rgba(128, 55, 12, 128)
    ---
    --- print(Color.red(data.value)) -- 255
    --- ```
    color: @checked () -> DataValueColor,
}

--- Represents a listener callback that can observe changes on an object.
--- See Property addListener and PropertyTrigger addListener.
export type Listener<T> = <K>(self:T, obj:K, (K)->()) -> () & (self:T, ()->()) -> ()

--- Represents a mutable property that stores a value and supports change listeners.
export type Property<T> = {
    --- The current value of the property.
    ---
    --- You can both read and assign to this field.
    --- ```lua
    --- local health = vm:getNumber("health")
    ---
    --- if health then
    ---   print(health.value) -- read
    ---   health.value = 100  -- write
    --- end
    --- ```
    value: T,

    --- Registers a listener that is called whenever the property's value changes.
    ---
    --- This function has two signatures:
    --- - `addListener(callback)` — Simple form, just pass the callback function.
    --- - `addListener(anchor, callback)` — Pass an anchor object and a callback.
    ---   The anchor is stored alongside the listener and passed to the callback
    ---   when invoked. This is useful for preventing garbage collection of objects
    ---   you need to keep alive while the listener is active.
    ---
    --- **Important:** If you obtain a ViewModel or property using a local variable
    --- (e.g., `local vm = context:viewModel()`) and add listeners without storing
    --- the ViewModel elsewhere, it may be garbage collected after the function
    --- returns. To prevent this, either:
    --- - Store the ViewModel on `self` (e.g., `self.vm = context:viewModel()`)
    --- - Pass the ViewModel as the anchor parameter to `addListener`
    ---
    --- ```lua
    --- local health = vm:getNumber("health")
    ---
    --- if health then
    ---   local function onHealthChanged(prop)
    ---     print("New health:", prop.value)
    ---   end
    ---
    ---   health:addListener(onHealthChanged)
    ---
    ---   health.value = 50 -- Triggers listener
    --- end
    --- ```
    ---
    --- Using the anchor parameter to keep the ViewModel alive:
    --- ```lua
    --- local vm = context:viewModel()
    --- local health = vm:getNumber("health")
    ---
    --- if health then
    ---   health:addListener(vm, function(anchor)
    ---     -- 'anchor' is the vm we passed, kept alive by the listener
    ---     print("Health changed!")
    ---   end)
    --- end
    --- ```
    addListener: Listener<Property<T>>,

    --- Removes a previously registered listener.
    ---
    --- This function has two signatures:
    --- - `removeListener(callback)` — Pass the callback function to remove.
    --- - `removeListener(anchor, callback)` — Pass an anchor and the callback.
    ---   The anchor parameter is accepted for API symmetry with `addListener`,
    ---   but only the callback is used for matching.
    ---
    --- ```lua
    --- local health = vm:getNumber("health")
    ---
    --- if health then
    ---   local function onHealthChanged(prop)
    ---     print("New health:", prop.value)
    ---     health:removeListener(onHealthChanged)
    ---   end
    ---
    ---   health:addListener(onHealthChanged)
    ---
    ---   health.value = 50 -- Triggers listener
    --- end
    --- ```
    removeListener: Listener<Property<T>>,
}

--- Represents a trigger property that can fire events and notify listeners.
--- Unlike other `Property` types, a trigger does not store a persistent value. It emits an event when fire() is called.
export type PropertyTrigger = {

    --- Registers a listener that is invoked when the trigger fires.
    ---
    --- This function has two signatures:
    --- - `addListener(callback)` — Simple form, just pass the callback function.
    --- - `addListener(anchor, callback)` — Pass an anchor object and a callback.
    ---   The anchor is stored alongside the listener and passed to the callback
    ---   when invoked. This is useful for preventing garbage collection of objects
    ---   you need to keep alive while the listener is active.
    ---
    --- **Important:** If you obtain a ViewModel or property using a local variable
    --- (e.g., `local vm = context:viewModel()`) and add listeners without storing
    --- the ViewModel elsewhere, it may be garbage collected after the function
    --- returns. To prevent this, either:
    --- - Store the ViewModel on `self` (e.g., `self.vm = context:viewModel()`)
    --- - Pass the ViewModel as the anchor parameter to `addListener`
    ---
    --- ```lua
    --- local vmi = context:viewModel()
    --- if vmi then
    ---   local cannon = vmi:getTrigger('cannon')
    ---   if cannon then
    ---     cannon:addListener(function()
    ---       print("cannon fired!")
    ---     end)
    ---
    ---     cannon:fire()
    ---   end
    --- end
    --- ```
    ---
    --- Using the anchor parameter to keep the ViewModel alive:
    --- ```lua
    --- local vm = context:viewModel()
    --- if vm then
    ---   local cannon = vm:getTrigger('cannon')
    ---   if cannon then
    ---     cannon:addListener(vm, function(anchor)
    ---       -- 'anchor' is the vm we passed, kept alive by the listener
    ---       print("cannon fired!")
    ---     end)
    ---   end
    --- end
    --- ```
    addListener: Listener<PropertyTrigger>,

    --- Removes a previously registered listener.
    --- Always remove listeners when they are no longer needed to avoid leaks.
    ---
    --- This function has two signatures:
    --- - `removeListener(callback)` — Pass the callback function to remove.
    --- - `removeListener(anchor, callback)` — Pass an anchor and the callback.
    ---   The anchor parameter is accepted for API symmetry with `addListener`,
    ---   but only the callback is used for matching.
    ---
    --- ```lua
    --- function init(self: MyNode, context: Context): boolean
    ---   local vmi = context:viewModel()
    ---   if vmi then
    ---     local cannon = vmi:getTrigger('cannon')
    ---     if cannon then
    ---       self.cannon = cannon
    ---       self.onCannonFired = onCannonFired
    ---       cannon:addListener(onCannonFired)
    ---     end
    ---   end
    ---
    ---   return true
    --- end
    ---
    --- function removeCannonListener(self: MyNode)
    ---   if self.cannon then
    ---     self.cannon:removeListener(self.onCannonFired)
    ---   end
    --- end
    --- ```
    removeListener: Listener<PropertyTrigger>,

    --- Fires the trigger and notifies all registered listeners.
    --- ```lua
    --- local vmi = context:viewModel()
    --- if vmi then
    ---   local cannon = vmi:getTrigger('cannon')
    ---   if cannon then
    ---     cannon:addListener(function()
    ---       print("cannon fired!")
    ---     end)
    ---
    ---     cannon:fire()
    ---   end
    --- end
    --- ```
    fire: (self:PropertyTrigger) -> (),
}
```
